name: Schrödinger ring track (128)
description: Saturable nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a painted potential V: a ring-shaped channel of low V (a circular optical waveguide, depth 0.6, 16 cells wide, radius 44 cells in a 128×128 field) guides solitons round and round. Two solitons chase each other clockwise, half a lap apart. In the lab they ran 10 laps in 60k steps without leaving the track. No absorbing border: the field wraps round, so the little light the solitons shed stays in play. (Sent head-on at this speed they don't pass cleanly: a collision can split off a third soliton.) Things to try: paint V (the params brush) to add tracks: negative V is a channel, positive V a wall that bounces solitons; paint a blob of positive V across the ring to make a reflector, or a gap to see one escape; the seed brush adds light, and a slow blob dropped on the track gets caught by it.
